notes:
POC scope: private VPC deployment (customer-managed AWS account). Priority: data residency (EU), auditability, KMS/HSM integration, minimal data egress.

Summary from discovery:
- Use-case: clinical triage + patient-facing support bot; document search over internal policies and anonymized records.
- Latency targets: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms for short prompts; conversational sessions avg 30 tokens/sec throughput target.
- Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay for private deployment if unit economics ~ within forecast range.
- Model preference: open models validated by Redwood catalog; customer wants ability to pin stable model SHAs. Also interested in lower-quantized variants for batch inference.

Security/compliance notes:
- Security questionnaire answered 2025-01-22; outstanding items: KMS integration pattern, audit log retention window, evidence of SOC2 controls for Private control plane.
- Must integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS with external key material). HSM integration discussed as optional future phase.
- Data residency: all persistent storage must remain in eu-central-1; ephemeral compute may be in other regions but no tokenization or logs exported.

POC technical plan (high level):
- Phase 0: Pre-reqs (NDA, DPA, AWS IAM role + cross-account access, VPC cadence).
- Phase 1: Terraform modules applied to customer's infra (VPC, subnets, security groups, ECR repos), values and templating in repo. PR: https://git.example.com/gfmi/redwood-poc (stub).
- Phase 2: Helm deploy of Redwood Private stack into customer's EKS cluster; set values: external_kms=true, audit_exporter.enabled=true, log_retention_days=365.
- Phase 3: Integration testing: smoke generation, streaming, KV-cache validation, model pinning, failover to hosted fallback disabled for security-first POC. Run perf harness and capture p99/p95.
- Phase 4: Security sign-off: customer InfoSec checklist, penetration test scheduling (if required), provide SOC2 artifacts and architecture diagram.
- Sign-off criteria: successful terraform apply + helm deploy, passing integration tests, audit logs present in S3 with correct encryption, KMS-managed keys used for storage and secrets, runbook for failover and rollback produced.

Customer quotes: "We need tight control over keys and audit trails — cannot have tokens persist outside our control." — Director of IT.

Short-term asks: SE session to finalize Terraform variables, legal to push DPA, network to provide VPC peering window (Feb 25-27).
